## Documentations/RM-EP-001.md

# Emergency Preparedness Program

---

## 1. Policy Header

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Policy ID | RM-EP-001 |
| Policy Title | Emergency Preparedness Program |
| Domain | RM — Risk Management & Safety |
| Subdomain | EP — Emergency Preparedness |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | Administrator / Risk Manager |
| Effective Date | 2026-04-01 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Approved By | Governing Body / Administrator — Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. |
| Last Reviewed | 2026-03-27 |
| Next Review Date | 2027-04-01 |
| Supersedes | N/A (Initial Version — consolidates EP elements from CL-PR-005, OP-FM-005, OP-SL-006, HR-TD-005) |

---

## 2. Purpose

This policy establishes the comprehensive Emergency Preparedness (EP) Program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. as required by 42 CFR §484.102 — Condition of Participation: Emergency Preparedness. This CoP is a standalone, separately surveyed Condition that requires a unified, documented EP program with all four required elements:

**(a) Risk assessment and EP plan** — an all-hazards approach based on the geographic service area's specific risks  
**(b) Policies and procedures** — detailing how services will be maintained through emergencies  
**(c) Communication plan** — for patients, staff, and external entities  
**(d) Training and testing** — including two exercises per year, at least one of which must incorporate an actual emergency event or a community-based exercise when available

CMS State Operations Manual Appendix B surveys emergency preparedness as a unified CoP. Fragmented coverage across individual policies (CL-PR-005, OP-FM-005, OP-SL-006, HR-TD-005) does not satisfy the CMS requirement for a documentable, integrated EP program. This policy serves as the governing EP Program document; the pre-existing policies remain in force and are cross-referenced as subcomponents.

---

## 3. Scope

This program applies to:

* All employees, contractors, volunteers, and students of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.
* All patients actively enrolled in care with the agency, from the date of admission through the date of discharge
* All operational sites: main office, any satellite/branch offices, and the full geographic service area in which home visits are conducted
* All emergency and disaster scenarios identified in the Risk Assessment (Section 6.1)

This program covers emergencies that require implementation of contingency operations, including but not limited to: natural disasters (earthquake, wildfire, flood, extreme heat events, mudslide), severe weather, public health emergencies (pandemic, disease outbreak, environmental contamination), terrorism or civil unrest, infrastructure failures (utility outages, building evacuations, telecommunications failure), and individual patient emergencies requiring care continuity.

---

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Emergency / Disaster | Any event, natural or man-made, that disrupts or threatens to disrupt the agency's ability to provide safe, effective care to patients or threatens the safety of staff. |
| All-Hazards Approach | An EP planning methodology that addresses a broad range of risks without specifying a single type of hazard — focusing on capabilities, roles, and communication that apply across risk types. Required by 42 CFR §484.102(a)(1)(i). |
| Incident Command System (ICS) | A standardized, hierarchical approach to emergency response management that establishes clear command authority, span of control, and communication protocols. The agency uses an ICS-based structure during declared emergencies. |
| Essential Patients | Patients in the agency's active caseload who require more frequent monitoring or have physical or cognitive limitations that make them particularly vulnerable during an emergency. Identified through the Vulnerability Assessment at admission per Section 6.2. |
| Alternate Care Site | A location, other than the patient's primary residence, where care could be coordinated or services temporarily provided if the patient's home is inaccessible during a disaster. |
| Business Continuity | The agency's capacity to maintain critical operations (patient care, billing, communications) during and after an emergency event. |
| After-Action Report (AAR) | A structured review of how the agency performed during an actual or simulated emergency, identifying gaps and improvements. Required after each training exercise. |
| Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) | The operational subplan detailing how the agency will sustain or rapidly restore essential services during and after an emergency. |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a comprehensive, written Emergency Preparedness Program that meets all four elements of 42 CFR §484.102 at all times. The program shall be based on an all-hazards risk assessment specific to the agency's geographic service area and patient population.

5.2 The Administrator is the designated EP Program Responsible Person. The Risk Manager is the operational EP coordinator. The Director of Nursing is responsible for clinical EP coordination. All three shall have designated alternates.

5.3 The EP Program shall be reviewed and updated no less than annually, and within 30 calendar days of any of the following: (a) a significant change in the agency's service area, patient population, or operations; (b) completion of an emergency exercise or response to an actual emergency that identifies program deficiencies; (c) a change in the regulatory EP requirements.

5.4 The agency shall conduct a minimum of two emergency preparedness exercises each calendar year: (a) at least one full-scale exercise, community-based exercise, or response to an actual emergency; and (b) at least one tabletop exercise, drills, or other exercise type, as an alternative. Where the agency participates in a community-based exercise, this shall count as the full-scale exercise requirement.

5.5 All employees shall receive EP-specific training at orientation and at least annually thereafter, sufficient to enable them to execute their roles in the EP plan.

5.6 The Governing Body shall review and approve the EP Program annually per GV-GB-001, Section 6.2.6.

---

## 6. Procedures

### 6.1 All-Hazards Risk Assessment

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.1.1 | Administrator / Risk Manager | Conduct a written all-hazards risk assessment covering the agency's full geographic service area. The assessment shall identify: (a) natural hazards likely in the service area (Los Angeles / Southern California context: earthquake, wildfire, flood, landslide, extreme heat event, Southern California Edison Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) events, Santa Ana wind events); (b) man-made hazards (power grid failure, civil unrest, terrorism, regional contamination, water supply disruption); (c) public health hazards (pandemic influenza, novel pathogen emergence, regional outbreak); (d) technology hazards (EHR system failure, cybersecurity incident, telecommunications outage). | Completed annually; initial assessment within 30 days of program adoption. |
| 6.1.2 | Risk Manager | For each identified hazard, assess: (a) likelihood of occurrence (Low/Medium/High based on CalOES Hazard Mitigation Plan data for the service area); (b) potential impact on patient care operations (Low/Medium/High); (c) existing controls mitigating the risk. | As part of annual risk assessment. |
| 6.1.3 | Administrator | Use the risk assessment findings to prioritize EP planning: highest-likelihood + highest-impact hazards shall have specific, more detailed procedures in the EP plan. Low-likelihood / low-impact hazards are covered under the general all-hazards protocols. | At adoption; annually updated. |
| 6.1.4 | Director of Nursing | Integrate the community hazard assessment into the patient vulnerability assessment process (Section 6.2) to identify which patients are most at risk from the identified hazards. | Annual integration with risk assessment cycle. |

### 6.2 Patient Vulnerability Assessment and Prioritization

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.2.1 | Admitting Clinician | At admission, complete the Patient Emergency Preparedness Vulnerability Assessment (Appendix A) for every patient. The assessment shall document: (a) patient reliance on electrically powered medical equipment (ventilator, oxygen concentrator, IV infusion pump, electric hospital bed, stair lift); (b) patient mobility limitations (non-ambulatory, wheelchair-dependent, unable to self-evacuate); (c) patient cognitive limitations affecting self-protective action; (d) patient's access to emergency contacts or caregivers; (e) geographic risk of the patient's location (flood zone, high fire hazard area, hillside property). | At admission; reviewed at each recertification or significant change in condition. |
| 6.2.2 | Director of Nursing | Maintain a current list of all Essential Patients (those with electric-dependent equipment, no self-evacuation capacity, or living alone with cognitive impairment). This list shall be updated in the care management system within 24 hours of any change in patient status, and shall be available to the on-call nurse at all times. | Maintained continuously; updated within 24 hours of change. |
| 6.2.3 | Scheduler / Director of Nursing | Register patients with electrically powered life-sustaining equipment with their utility provider's Medical Baseline or Life Support program and with the local public safety agency's Access and Functional Needs (AFN) registry where available. Document registration in the patient record. | Within 14 days of admission for qualifying patients. |
| 6.2.4 | Director of Nursing | During any declared emergency or Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) event: activate the Essential Patients contact protocol — direct care staff to attempt contact with all Essential Patients within 4 hours of emergency declaration; document contact attempts and patient status. | Within 4 hours of emergency activation. |

### 6.3 EP Policies and Procedures — Continuity of Care

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.3.1 | Administrator / Director of Nursing | Maintain written Continuity of Care Procedures (Appendix B) covering at minimum: (a) how scheduled visits will be prioritized and rescheduled during emergency-related service disruption; (b) how Essential Patients will be triaged for available staff capacity; (c) how abbreviated clinical visits or telephone check-ins will be authorized as an emergency substitution; (d) criteria for suspending vs. continuing services to patients in affected areas; (e) procedures for coordinating with discharging hospitals or receiving facilities if patients must be evacuated or hospitalized. | Current procedures maintained as Appendix B; reviewed annually and after each exercise. |
| 6.3.2 | Administrator | Maintain written Office/Operations Continuity Procedures (Appendix C) covering: (a) ability to process payroll, benefits, and employee communications when the main office is inaccessible; (b) access to EHR when primary server or internet is unavailable (identify alternate access method, e.g., mobile hotspot, printed backup schedule, EHR vendor's offline mode); (c) backup contact lists for all staff and key Agencies (accreditation body, Medicare administrative contractor, CDPH, local emergency management); (d) procedure for operating from an alternate site if the main office is uninhabitable. | Current procedures maintained as Appendix C; reviewed annually. |
| 6.3.3 | Director of Nursing | Maintain written procedures for how clinical documentation will be captured and preserved during an EHR or telecommunications outage, including: (a) use of agency-approved paper documentation forms; (b) required elements to be transcribed into EHR within 24 hours of service restoration; (c) chain of custody for paper records generated during outage. | Current procedures maintained as Appendix B; reviewed annually. |
| 6.3.4 | Risk Manager | Ensure the agency maintains minimum operational supply levels at all times including: (a) 72-hour supply of commonly used clinical supplies (wound dressings, IV supplies, medication management supplies) distributable to Essential Patients if resupply is disrupted; (b) 72-hour supply of PPE; (c) backup communication devices (charged portable mobile devices for key staff). | Supplies maintained at minimum levels; reviewed quarterly. |

### 6.4 Emergency Communication Plan

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.4.1 | Administrator | Maintain a current, printed Emergency Contact Directory (Appendix D) that is distributed to all supervisors and updated at least annually (or within 14 days of any contact change). The directory must contain: (a) All agency staff with primary and secondary phone contact methods; (b) Governing Body members; (c) Medicare Administrative Contractor (CGS or Palmetto, as applicable); (d) California Department of Public Health HCAI regional contact; (e) Cal OES State Operations Center (916-845-8911); (f) Local emergency management agency; (g) Local fire and law enforcement non-emergency lines; (h) HHA accreditation body (if applicable); (i) Key vendors (medical supply, pharmacy, EHR vendor). | Maintained continuously; distributed to all supervisors; updated within 14 days of change. |
| 6.4.2 | Administrator | Establish and document the staff notification tree for emergency activation: (a) Risk Manager notifies Department Heads; (b) Department Heads notify all assigned staff via the agency's designated mass-notification method (phone tree, text broadcast, or EHR notification); (c) confirm receipt and availability of all staff is documented on the Staff Notification Log (Appendix E). | Protocol established; tested in each annual exercise. |
| 6.4.3 | Director of Nursing | Establish the patient notification procedure for emergency disruption: (a) if scheduled visits cannot be made, notify the patient (or caregiver) by phone no later than 2 hours before the scheduled visit time; (b) provide safety guidance matching the emergency type (e.g., shelter-in-place, evacuation route resources); (c) document all patient contacts and outcomes in the Emergency Patient Contact Log (Appendix F). | Upon emergency activation; contact within 2 hours of missed visit. |
| 6.4.4 | Administrator | Identify and document the agency's alternate communication methods in the event of phone system and internet outage simultaneously: designated emergency FM radio station for public alerts; agency-issued satellite phone or satellite communicator for Administrator and Risk Manager; walkie-talkie/radio for on-site staff if main office is occupied during civil event. | Documented in EP plan; devices maintained and charged. |
| 6.4.5 | Administrator | When an emergency disrupts normal operations for more than 24 hours, notify the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) per MAC guidance for the affected geographic area. Document the notification and retain in the EP file. | Within 24 hours of extended operational disruption. |

### 6.5 Training and Testing

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.5.1 | Risk Manager / Training Coordinator | Provide EP training to all new employees as part of orientation, before they begin patient care duties, covering: (a) their specific role in the EP plan; (b) the patient vulnerability assessment and Essential Patients protocol; (c) communication tree and staff notification procedure; (d) emergency supply location; (e) ICS structure during emergencies; (f) how to report an emergency and what to do if they are isolated during a disaster. | At orientation, before first clinical duties. |
| 6.5.2 | Risk Manager / Training Coordinator | Provide annual EP refresher training to all employees covering: (a) post-exercise lessons learned from the prior year; (b) any EP plan changes; (c) regulatory updates; (d) a scenario-based rapid runthrough of a specific emergency type. | Annually; completed within calendar year. |
| 6.5.3 | Risk Manager | Plan and execute at least two emergency preparedness exercises per calendar year (per 42 CFR §484.102(d)): (a) Exercise Type 1 — full-scale exercise, community-based exercise, OR an actual emergency response that is documented and reviewed as an exercise equivalent; (b) Exercise Type 2 — tabletop exercise with agency leadership and clinical managers, or structured drills. Both exercise types shall test the communication plan and EP procedures. | Two exercises per calendar year; at least one full-scale or community-based. |
| 6.5.4 | Risk Manager | Complete a written After-Action Report (AAR) within 30 calendar days of each exercise or actual emergency response. The AAR shall document: (a) scenario used; (b) participants; (c) strengths identified; (d) gaps or failures identified; (e) corrective actions with assigned responsible party and completion deadline; (f) plan or procedure updates required. | Within 30 days of each exercise or emergency response. |
| 6.5.5 | Risk Manager | Implement all corrective actions identified in AARs within the timeframe specified in the AAR. Unresolved corrective actions shall be escalated to the Administrator at the next management meeting. | Per AAR-specified deadlines. |
| 6.5.6 | Administrator | Present the annual EP program review, exercise results, and AAR summaries to the Governing Body for review and approval, per GV-GB-001 Section 6.2.6. The Governing Body shall review and approve the EP plan annually. | At the Governing Body's third quarterly meeting each calendar year. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Actual emergency event declared in the service area | Risk Manager activates ICS; Administrator assumes Incident Commander role. | Execute EP communication plan. Activate Essential Patient contact protocol. Document all actions in real-time on the Emergency Operations Log. | Immediately upon declaration. |
| Annual program review not completed by due date | Risk Manager notifies Administrator. | Emergency completion convened within 14 days. Reason documented. Notify MAC if regulatory deadline is at risk. | 14 days. |
| CMS survey finds EP deficiency | Administrator convenes action meeting within 48 hours. | Develop Plan of Correction per CMS timelines. Risk Manager leads all EP corrective actions. Weekly status reports to Governing Body until resolved. | Plan of Correction per CMS-specified deadline. |
| Community-based exercise opportunity not available in a calendar year | Administrator documents unavailability in EP file. | Conduct internal full-scale exercise as substitute; document basis for substitution per CMS guidance. | In lieu of community exercise if none available. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Written EP program covers all 4 elements of 42 CFR §484.102 | Annual review against CMS Appendix B EP survey protocol | All 4 elements documented and current |
| Annual risk assessment completed | Review of risk assessment document | Completed within 12 months; service-area specific |
| Patient Vulnerability Assessments completed at admission | Audit of 10% of admission records quarterly | 100% completed at admission |
| Two exercises conducted annually with AARs on file | Review of exercise documentation and AARs | 2 exercises per calendar year; AARs within 30 days each |
| All EP corrective actions (from AARs) completed on time | Review of AAR corrective action tracker | 100% closed by assigned deadline |
| All employees trained at orientation and annually | Training log audit | 100% at orientation; 100% annual rate within calendar year |
| Governing Body approval of EP plan documented | Review of Governing Body minutes | Annual approval documented at third quarterly meeting |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

CMS surveyors conducting an Emergency Preparedness survey under the State Operations Manual Appendix B will specifically verify:

1. That a single, integrated EP program document exists covering all four required elements — not four separate policies. Surveyors are trained to ask for "your Emergency Preparedness Plan" and will note fragmentation as a program deficiency.
2. That the risk assessment was based on the agency's specific geographic service area — not a generic template. For agencies in Southern California, surveyors know the region's hazards (earthquake, wildfire, Santa Ana winds, PSPS events) and will probe whether the plan addresses them.
3. That the patient vulnerability assessment is documented for all active patients and that an Essential Patients list is maintained in real-time.
4. That two exercises were conducted in the prior calendar year, with written AARs. Missing an exercise year, or conducting an exercise without an AAR, is a common citation.
5. That staff can describe their role in the EP plan consistently with what's documented.
6. That the communication plan is written, tested, and includes all required external contacts.
7. Governing Body approval of the EP plan is documented in board minutes.

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Fragmented EP coverage across 4+ policies with no governing EP Program document | CMS Condition-level deficiency — failure to have an EP Program | This policy (RM-EP-001) is the governing EP Program; the 4 existing policies are incorporated as cross-references/subcomponents |
| Risk assessment is generic (not service-area specific) | Surveyor rejects non-specific plan as non-compliant | Section 6.1 specifically addresses Southern California hazard profile |
| Essential Patients list not maintained in real-time | Critical patients unidentified during actual emergency | DON responsible for 24-hr update of list; on-call access required |
| Only one exercise conducted per year, not two | CoP deficiency | Annual exercise calendar set by January 15; two exercises planned; AARs required within 30 days |
| AAR completed but corrective actions not tracked or implemented | Recurring deficiencies across exercise years | AAR corrective action tracker maintained; escalated to Administrator if overdue |
| No documentation that patients were contacted during an exercise | Surveyor cannot verify communication plan was tested | Communication plan testing explicitly required in exercise script; Appendix F log completed |

## 2. Purpose

This policy constitutes the written Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., as required by California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 8, §3203. A written IIPP is mandated for ALL California employers regardless of size, industry classification, or number of employees. The IIPP is the foundational Cal/OSHA compliance document from which all other occupational safety programs at this agency derive their authority and structure.

This program establishes:
- The identity of the person responsible for implementing and maintaining the IIPP;
- The system used to ensure compliance with safe and healthy work practice requirements;
- The system for communicating with employees about occupational health and safety;
- The procedures for identifying and evaluating workplace hazards;
- The procedures for investigating occupational injuries, illnesses, and near-misses;
- The methods for correcting identified hazards in a timely manner;
- The training and instruction program;
- The recordkeeping requirements.

This IIPP applies to the entirety of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.'s operations, including office environments and all field operations in patient residences and community settings.

---

## 3. Scope

This program applies to:
* All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. in all roles (clinical, administrative, supportive)
* All work locations: the agency's main office, any branch offices, all patient homes and community settings where employees perform services
* Per Diem, contract, and temporary employees performing services on behalf of the agency
* Supervisors, managers, and senior leadership in their obligation to enforce and model safe work practices

This IIPP does not supersede the more specific Cal/OSHA programs required by separate provisions of Title 8:
- RM-OS-002 (ATD Exposure Control Plan — 8 CCR §5199)
- RM-OS-003 (Bloodborne Pathogen Exposure Control Plan — 8 CCR §5193)
- RM-OS-004 (Heat Illness Prevention Program — 8 CCR §3395/§5141.1)
- RM-SS-002 (Workplace Violence Prevention Plan — Cal. Labor Code §6401.9 / SB 553) — note: the WVPP is an appendix to this IIPP per SB 553

Those programs are cross-referenced in Section 10 and incorporated herein by reference as required subprograms of this master IIPP.

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| IIPP | Injury and Illness Prevention Program — the written, comprehensive workplace health and safety program required by 8 CCR §3203 for all California employers. |
| Cal/OSHA | California Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), also referred to as DOSH — the California agency responsible for enforcing Title 8 occupational safety regulations. |
| Hazard | Any condition, practice, or behavior in the workplace that poses a risk of injury, illness, or death to employees. Includes physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic, and psychosocial hazards. |
| Corrective Action | Steps taken to eliminate or control an identified hazard, including engineering controls, administrative controls, and personal protective equipment (PPE) in the hierarchy of controls. |
| Responsible Person | The individual designated by the employer as responsible for implementing and maintaining the IIPP. At this agency, the Responsible Person is the Administrator, with the Risk Manager serving as the designated operational lead. |
| Near-Miss | Any event that could have resulted in injury or illness to an employee but did not, by chance or corrective action. Near-misses must be investigated and documented. |
| Imminent Hazard | A hazard that presents an immediate risk of death or serious physical harm to employees that cannot be eliminated through standard work practices without immediate corrective action. |
| Injury & Illness (I&I) Log | The OSHA 300 Log (Form 300) used to record all work-related injuries and illnesses throughout the year, as required by 8 CCR §14300. |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a written, implemented, and current Injury and Illness Prevention Program meeting all requirements of California Code of Regulations, Title 8, §3203.

5.2 The Administrator is the designated Responsible Person for this IIPP. The Risk Manager (or Administrator Designee) is the operational lead for day-to-day IIPP implementation, hazard assessments, training coordination, and recordkeeping.

5.3 All employees are required to comply with safe and healthful work practices identified in this IIPP and its associated subprograms. Employees who fail to follow safety requirements are subject to progressive disciplinary action per HR-ER-002.

5.4 The agency shall not retaliate against any employee who reports a workplace hazard, near-miss, injury, or illness in good faith. Retaliation against an employee for exercising rights under Cal/OSHA or this IIPP is prohibited and may result in termination per HR-ER-005 and HR-ER-003.

5.5 This IIPP shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, or whenever:
- A new job processes, procedures, or equipment are introduced that create new hazards;
- A workplace injury, illness, or near-miss investigation reveals a program deficiency;
- A Cal/OSHA inspection results in a citation;
- New Cal/OSHA regulations affect the agency's operations.

5.6 The agency shall provide effective safety and health training to all employees in a language and at a literacy level understandable to the employee.

5.7 The agency shall maintain records of IIPP implementation, inspections, training, incident investigations, and hazard corrections for a minimum of 5 years or as required by applicable regulation, whichever is longer.

The investigation must identify: (a) root cause; (b) contributing factors; (c) hazard controls to prevent recurrence. | Investigation initiated within 24 hours; written report within 5 business days. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Written IIPP exists, is current, and contains all 8 required elements | Annual review against 8 CCR §3203 checklist | All 8 elements present; reviewed and signed within the last 12 months |
| Annual hazard assessment completed | Review of dated Hazard Assessment Report | Completed annually; no more than 12 months since last assessment |
| Quarterly office inspections conducted | Review of inspection log dates and documentation | 4 inspections documented per calendar year |
| All newly hired employees received safety training before hazard exposure | Review of Safety Training Log; verify date vs. hire date | 100% trained before first hazard exposure |
| Annual safety refresher completed | Training completion rate | 100% of employees within calendar year |
| Incidents investigated within 5 business days | Review of Incident Investigation Forms | 100% of qualifying incidents investigated within 5 days |
| Cal/OSHA reportable incidents reported within required timeframes | Review of reporting log | 100% reported within regulatory deadlines |
| Form 300 maintained and posted | Review of Form 300 log and posting evidence | Form 300 maintained; Form 300A posted Feb 1–Apr 30 annually |
| Hazard corrections completed within classified timeframes | Review of Hazard Correction Log | 100% Imminent (same-day), Serious (24 hours), Moderate (7 days), Minor (30 days) |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

Cal/OSHA compliance officers conducting a workplace inspection will specifically verify:

1. The written IIPP document exists, is current, and is available at the workplace. The absence of a written IIPP is a General Industry Safety Order violation with potential civil penalty.
2. The Responsible Person is clearly identified by name and title. An IIPP that identifies a generic "HR" or "Safety Officer" who is not specifically named is inadequate.
3. Records of hazard assessments, safety inspections, incident investigations, and corrective actions are maintained and accessible.
4. Employees can confirm they received safety training and know how to report hazards. Cal/OSHA may interview employees to verify IIPP effectiveness.
5. The Form 300 Log is properly maintained and all recordable incidents are entered correctly.
6. All required subprogram ECPs (BBP, ATD, Workplace Violence) are incorporated by reference and exist as separate written programs.
7. The IIPP is available in a language understandable to non-English-speaking employees.

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| IIPP exists only as a template with no agency-specific customization | Cal/OSHA citation; penalty | This document is Agency-specific; all roles, contacts, and procedures reference Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. specifically |
| Responsible Person is generic (HR/Safety) not named | Citation | Administrator named as Responsible Person; Risk Manager named as operational lead in this document |
| No field-specific hazard assessment (only office hazards assessed) | Citation; unprotected field staff | Field Visit Safety Checklist (Appendix D) addresses home environment hazards specifically |
| Incident investigation form exists but not consistently used | Missed near-misses; no trend analysis | Training and supervisor compliance assurance procedures enforce form completion |
| Safety training records not maintained separately | Cannot demonstrate training in Cal/OSHA inspection | Safety Training Log (Appendix G) maintained by Training Coordinator, separate from general HR file |
| Form 300 not maintained because "we had no recordable injuries" | Form 300 must be maintained even if zero entries | Form 300 maintained with zero entries where applicable |

# Aerosol Transmissible Disease (ATD) Exposure Control Plan

## 2. Purpose

This document constitutes the written Aerosol Transmissible Disease (ATD) Exposure Control Plan for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., as required by the California Code of Regulations, Title 8, §5199 — Aerosol Transmissible Diseases Standard. Home health agencies are explicitly designated as "ATD-susceptible workplaces" under 8 CCR §5199(a)(5) because employees routinely enter residences and provide direct patient care where aerosol transmissible pathogens may be present.

This plan establishes the specific protections, procedures, and responsibilities required for employees whose work creates a risk of exposure to aerosol transmissible pathogens including, but not limited to:
- Mycobacterium tuberculosis (TB)
- SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) and variants
- Measles (Rubeola)
- Chickenpox/Varicella
- Influenza (during periods of declared epidemic or outbreak)
- Monkeypox/Mpox
- Any other pathogen designated as an ATD under 8 CCR §5199(a)(1)

This ECP is an appendix to and subprogram of RM-OS-001 (IIPP). It does not replace CL-SD-016 (Infection Prevention & Control), which governs patient care IPC standards. This ECP governs EMPLOYEE occupational safety obligations specifically.

---

## 3. Scope

This plan applies to:

* All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who may have occupational exposure to aerosol transmissible pathogens in the course of their work duties
* All work settings: patient residences, group homes, skilled nursing facilities visited for care coordination, and the agency's office if a clinical activity occurs there
* Specific job classifications with potential ATD occupational exposure: Registered Nurse (RN), Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN), Physical Therapist (PT), Occupational Therapist (OT), Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP), Medical Social Worker (MSW), Home Health Aide (HHA), Intake Coordinator (if conducting in-home assessments)

Administrative staff with no patient-facing duties in clinical settings are covered by ATD general precaution requirements but are not classified as ATD-exposed workers under 8 CCR §5199(a)(4).

---

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| ATD | Aerosol Transmissible Disease — an infectious disease transmitted through airborne droplet nuclei or droplets, as listed in Appendix D of 8 CCR §5199. |
| ATD Exposure Control Plan (ECP) | A written, site-specific document detailing the employer's procedures for identifying and controlling occupational ATD exposure risks, as required by 8 CCR §5199(c). |
| Airborne Infectious Isolation (AII) | Procedures and conditions required to safely care for a patient known or suspected to have an airborne transmissible ATD, including appropriate respiratory protection, patient placement, and ventilation. |
| Respiratory Protection Program | The employer's program for ensuring that employees are properly fit-tested for and provided with appropriate respiratory protective equipment (NIOSH-approved N95 or higher) per 8 CCR §5144. |
| Fit Testing | The mandatory OSHA/Cal/OSHA protocol used to verify that a specific respirator model creates an effective seal on an individual employee's face, conducted before initial use and at least annually. |
| ATD Exposure Incident | A specific eye, mouth, mucous membrane, or respiratory tract exposure to an ATD pathogen through contact that creates a potential for infection during a specific episode. |
| Aerosol-Generating Procedure (AGP) | A clinical procedure that generates airborne particles, including suctioning, nebulizer treatments, high-flow oxygen, CPR, and certain oral/respiratory care procedures. |
| ATD-Susceptible Workplace | A work location where employees, due to the nature of their duties, are at elevated risk for ATD exposure — home health agencies are explicitly classified as ATD-susceptible workplaces per 8 CCR §5199(a)(5). |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a current, written ATD Exposure Control Plan meeting all requirements of 8 CCR §5199 for all workers with potential ATD occupational exposure.

5.2 The agency shall determine, document, and maintain an ATD Exposure Determination identifying, by job classification, all employees with potential occupational ATD exposure. All employees in clinical roles listed in Section 3 are classified as ATD-exposed workers.

5.3 The agency shall provide, at no cost to the employee, appropriate respiratory protective equipment — minimum NIOSH-approved N95 respirator — whenever an employee may encounter a patient with a known or suspected ATD. The agency shall also provide surgical/procedure masks for all field visits as a minimum standard.

5.4 The agency shall maintain a Respiratory Protection Program that meets all requirements of 8 CCR §5144, including initial medical evaluation, fit testing, and annual re-fit testing for all employees assigned N95 respirators.

5.5 The agency shall ensure employees are medically cleared for respirator use before being required to use an N95 or higher respirator, using the OSHA Medical Evaluation Questionnaire per 29 CFR §1910.134(e).

5.6 The agency shall provide ATD-specific exposure investigation, post-exposure medical evaluation, and follow-up at no cost to the employee, within timeframes specified in Section 6.5.

5.7 All employees with potential ATD occupational exposure shall receive ATD-specific training that meets the content requirements of 8 CCR §5199(g) before initial assignment and annually thereafter.

5.8 This ECP shall be reviewed and updated at least annually or whenever a new ATD is identified as a significant occupational risk (e.g., a public health emergency declaration), a change in agency operations creates new ATD exposures, or a post-exposure investigation reveals a program gap.

5.9 This ECP is a subprogram of RM-OS-001 (IIPP) and does not conflict with CL-SD-016 (Infection Prevention & Control). Where both apply, the more protective standard governs employee occupational safety.

---

## 6. Procedures

### 6.1 ATD Exposure Determination

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing / Risk Manager | Conduct and document an ATD Exposure Determination that identifies, by job classification, all employees with potential occupational ATD exposure without regard to personal protective equipment. Attach the Exposure Determination Table (Appendix A) to this ECP. | At ECP adoption; reviewed and confirmed annually. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing | For each identified job classification, document the specific ATD exposure pathways: (a) direct patient care involving respiratory assessment; (b) aerosol-generating procedures (suctioning, nebulizer, oxygen therapy, CPR); (c) presence in confined spaces (small rooms) with ATD patients without adequate ventilation; (d) transport of patients with ATD. | At ECP adoption; reviewed and confirmed annually. |
| 6.1.3 | Risk Manager | When a new clinical role or service line is established, conduct a supplemental Exposure Determination within 30 days of service introduction to assess ATD exposure risk for the new role. Update Appendix A accordingly. | Within 30 days of new service introduction. |

### 6.2 ATD Precaution Procedures — All Field Visits

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.2.1 | Scheduling / Intake Coordinator | During scheduling, screen for ATD risk indicators by verifying with referral source and patient/caregiver: (a) known or suspected active TB; (b) known COVID-19 positive status; (c) known varicella, measles, or other listed ATD; (d) immunocompromised household members who may be especially affected. Flag high-risk visits in the scheduling system. | At time of scheduling and at each visit authorization. |
| 6.2.2 | Field Clinical Staff | Upon arrival at every patient residence, perform a brief respiratory symptom screen before entering: ask the patient and/or caregiver if anyone in the home has respiratory symptoms (cough, fever, shortness of breath), known COVID-19, TB, or other respiratory illness in the prior 14 days. Document findings in the patient visit note. | Before each visit entry. |
| 6.2.3 | Field Clinical Staff | For ALL visits: don a surgical/procedure mask before patient contact. Agency shall supply masks to all field staff. Masks shall not be reused across multiple patient visits or across days. | Every visit. |
| 6.2.4 | Field Clinical Staff | For visits flagged as high-risk ATD per 6.2.1 OR where 6.2.2 screening identifies active symptoms: don NIOSH-approved fit-tested N95 respirator (from personal supply issued by agency) before entering the area where the patient resides. Don appropriate eye protection (goggles or face shield) if performing AGPs or mucous membrane contact is anticipated. | High-risk visits; symptomatic household visits. |
| 6.2.5 | Field Clinical Staff | If an AGP (e.g., suctioning, nebulizer treatment, CPR, high-flow oxygen) is performed: wear N95 or higher respirator regardless of patient ATD status. Position patient to maximize ventilation away from the clinician when possible. | Whenever performing an AGP, regardless of known ATD status. |
| 6.2.6 | Field Clinical Staff | Perform proper donning, doffing, and disposal of respiratory PPE per agency PPE training. Sanitize hands after doffing. If N95 is damaged, soiled, or has compromised fit, remove and replace; notify scheduler for additional supplies. | Every visit. |

### 6.3 Respiratory Protection Program

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.3.1 | Risk Manager | Maintain a current NIOSH-approved N95 respirator model(s) on the agency's approved respirator list. Select models for which medical evaluation and fit testing will be conducted. Do not use KN95 respirators as OSHA-compliant respiratory protection in occupational settings (KN95 is not NIOSH-approved). | Continuous; annual review. |
| 6.3.2 | Risk Manager / HR | Before assigning any employee to a role requiring N95 respirator use, administer the OSHA Medical Evaluation Questionnaire (29 CFR §1910.134 Appendix C) to identify any medical conditions that might interfere with respirator use. Route questionnaire responses to the designated PLHCP (Physician or Licensed Health Care Professional) for review. Employees with medical conditions identified by the PLHCP shall be medically cleared before N95 use. | Before initial assignment to N95-required duties. |
| 6.3.3 | Risk Manager | Conduct initial qualitative or quantitative fit testing for all employees assigned to N95 use using a NIOSH-approved testing protocol and the specific N95 model the employee will wear. Document fit test results on the Fit Test Record (Appendix B). Employees who fail fit testing with the agency's standard model shall be evaluated for alternative models. | Before initial N95 use; at least annually. |
| 6.3.4 | Risk Manager | Conduct annual re-fit testing for all N95-assigned employees. Re-fit testing is also required if any of the following occur: (a) employee reports the respirator no longer fits; (b) employee undergoes significant dental or facial changes; (c) employee gains or loses more than 20 lbs; (d) employee undergoes facial surgical procedures. | Annually; upon triggering conditions listed. |
| 6.3.5 | Risk Manager | Maintain an adequate supply of issued N95 respirators to field staff. Track issuance. Ensure field staff replace N95s that are damp, soiled, physically damaged, or have perceived loss of seal. Field staff shall not reuse respirators across visits unless the respirator model is rated for extended use — document such models specifically. | Continuous supply management; document issuance. |
| 6.3.6 | Risk Manager | Evaluate respirator use performance at least annually: review fit test records, supply consumption, any incidents related to respiratory exposure, and employee feedback. Update respiratory protection program annually. | Annually. |

### 6.4 TB-Specific Controls

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.4.1 | Director of Nursing / HR | Ensure TB screening of all newly hired employees per HR-WM-003 (Employee Health & Immunization Requirements). A 2-step tuberculin skin test (TST) or IGRA blood test documents baseline TB status. | At hire; before direct patient contact. |
| 6.4.2 | Director of Nursing | Assess each patient's TB risk during intake using the standard TB Risk Assessment tool (Appendix C). Patients with active or suspected TB shall be so flagged in the care management system. | At intake; update with clinical changes. |
| 6.4.3 | Field Clinical Staff | For patients with known or suspected active TB: (a) confirm fit-tested N95 before entry; (b) ensure patient wears surgical mask if tolerated; (c) open windows if available and safe; (d) minimize time in confined spaces; (e) document ATD precautions taken in visit note. | Each visit for TB-flagged patients. |
| 6.4.4 | Director of Nursing | If a field employee reports potential exposure to a patient later confirmed to have active, infectious pulmonary TB: initiate ATD exposure investigation per Section 6.5. Notify Cal/OSHA if a work-related TB infection is identified. | Within 24 hours of notification of confirmed TB source. |

### 6.5 ATD Exposure Incident Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.5.1 | Exposed Employee | Report any potential ATD exposure incident to a supervisor and to the Director of Nursing immediately. An ATD exposure incident includes: (a) being in the same room for ≥15 minutes without appropriate respiratory protection with a person later confirmed to have an airborne ATD; (b) any unprotected AGP exposure. | Immediately upon recognition of exposure. |
| 6.5.2 | Director of Nursing / Risk Manager | Initiate an ATD Exposure Investigation within 24 hours: (a) document the date, time, location, and nature of exposure; (b) identify the source patient or individual; (c) determine whether ATD status of exposure source is known or suspect; (d) assess whether the employee's PPE was correctly donned during exposure. | Investigation initiated within 24 hours. |
| 6.5.3 | Risk Manager | Arrange post-exposure medical evaluation at the agency's designated occupational health provider at no cost to the employee. The evaluation must include: (a) assessment of exposure circumstances; (b) testing appropriate to the ATD (e.g., TB test, COVID test); (c) recommendations for prophylaxis where applicable (e.g., measles PEP); (d) work restriction assessment. | Post-exposure evaluation: within 24 hours for high-risk exposures; within 2 business days for moderate-risk. |
| 6.5.4 | Risk Manager | Document the exposure investigation and response on the ATD Exposure Incident Form (Appendix D). File in the employee's medical file (separate from personnel file per CMIA requirements — CO-CA-001, HR-WM-007). | Within 5 business days of incident; retain for duration of employment + 30 years per 8 CCR §5199(h). |
| 6.5.5 | Risk Manager | If the ATD exposure results in a work-related illness, record on the OSHA 300 Log (Form 300) per RM-OS-001 Section 6.5 and 8 CCR §14300. Report to Cal/OSHA if hospitalization or death results. | Recording: within 7 days of determination. Reporting: per RM-OS-001 thresholds. |
| 6.5.6 | Risk Manager / Director of Nursing | Conduct a root cause analysis of each ATD exposure incident (per QA-AE-002) to determine whether an ECP deficiency contributed to the exposure. Update the ECP or training within 30 days of the RCA findings. | RCA completed within 14 days; ECP/training update within 30 days. |

### 6.6 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Public health emergency declaring a novel ATD | Risk Manager notifies Administrator; monitors Cal/OSHA and CDPH guidance. | Update ECP within 30 days to incorporate novel pathogen-specific guidance. Provide emergent training to all field staff within 7 days of identified new risk. | ECP update: 30 days. Staff training: 7 days. |
| Employee refuses to wear N95 on ATD-flagged visit | Clinical Manager and Risk Manager notified. | Do not assign employee to that visit. Conduct counseling and retraining. HR-ER-002 discipline for refusal. Document. | Same day. Retraining within 5 business days. |
| N95 supply chain shortage | Risk Manager and Administrator escalate immediately. | Secure alternative NIOSH-approved respirator supply. Use hierarchy: N95 → KN95 (emergency use only with documentation of supply shortage) → proceed only with administrative controls if no respirator available and defer visit if clinical risk is tolerable. | Contingency plan activated within 24 hours of shortage identification. |
| Annual respirator fit test not completed for an employee | Risk Manager notifies employee and supervisor. | Employee may not perform ATD-risk visits until re-fit tested. Schedule within 14 days. | Re-fit test within 14 days of missed deadline. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Written ATD ECP exists and is current | Annual review against 8 CCR §5199 checklist | All required elements present; reviewed within 12 months |
| Exposure Determination completed and current | Review of Appendix A | All clinical job classifications assessed; reviewed annually |
| All N95-assigned employees medically cleared | Review of PLHCP clearance forms | 100% clearance documented before initial N95 use |
| All N95-assigned employees fit-tested annually | Review of fit test records (Appendix B) | 100% fit-tested within prior 12 months |
| N95s available at all ATD-flagged visits | Random field supply audit; employee survey | Employees confirm N95 is always available for high-risk visits |
| ATD exposure incidents investigated within timeframe | Review of Appendix D forms | 100% investigated within 24 hours of report |
| ATD-specific training completed | Training completion rate | 100% at orientation; 100% annual within calendar year |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

Cal/OSHA compliance officers will specifically verify:

1. That the ECP is written, site-specific, and not a generic template. The ATD ECP must reference the agency's specific operations, patient populations, and job classifications.
2. That an Exposure Determination has been completed identifying all at-risk job classifications.
3. Evidence that all N95-assigned employees are medically cleared and have current fit test documentation.
4. That ATD exposure incident records are maintained in the employee's confidential medical file (not personnel file).
5. Evidence of ATD-specific training at orientation and annually.
6. That the ECP is incorporated into the master IIPP (RM-OS-001) as a subprogram.

CMS surveyors examining Appendix B (Home Health CoPs) may cross-check ECP against condition-level Infection Prevention & Control requirements (42 CFR §484.70).

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| No Exposure Determination or generic "all employees" statement | Citation; does not identify actual exposure tasks | Appendix A specifies exposure by job class and by specific clinical activity |
| Staff using KN95s while claiming OSHA compliance | Cal/OSHA citation — KN95 is NOT NIOSH-approved for occupational use | Agency issues NIOSH-approved N95 only; training distinguishes N95 from KN95 |
| Fit test records not maintained or expired | Cal/OSHA citation; potential liability from exposure | Annual fit testing process tracked by Risk Manager; no ATD-flagged visits permitted for unfit-tested staff |
| ATD exposure records filed in personnel file | CMIA violation (Civil Code §56.20); Cal/OSHA violation | Medical exposure records filed in separate confidential medical file per CO-CA-001 |
| ECP not updated after public health emergency | Program gap for novel pathogens | CO-RA-001 monitoring triggers ECP review within 30 days of declared public health emergency |

# Bloodborne Pathogen (BBP) Exposure Control Plan

## 2. Purpose

This document constitutes the written Bloodborne Pathogen (BBP) Exposure Control Plan for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc., as required by California Code of Regulations, Title 8, §5193 — Bloodborne Pathogen Standard (substantially equivalent to, and in some respects more stringent than, OSHA 29 CFR §1910.1030). Home health agencies employ clinical staff who perform invasive procedures in uncontrolled patient residence environments, creating occupational bloodborne pathogen exposure risk among the highest across all healthcare settings.

This plan is designed to eliminate or minimize employee exposure to bloodborne pathogens including:
- Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)
- Hepatitis B Virus (HBV)
- Hepatitis C Virus (HCV)
- Any other pathogen that is present in human blood and can cause disease in humans

This ECP establishes the agency's exposure determination, methods of compliance, hepatitis B vaccination program, post-exposure evaluation and follow-up program, communication of hazards, recordkeeping, and annual review process.

This ECP is a subprogram of RM-OS-001 (IIPP). It does not replace CL-SD-016 (Infection Prevention & Control), which governs patient-centered IPC standards. This ECP governs EMPLOYEE occupational safety for BBP exposure prevention and response.

---

## 3. Scope

This plan applies to:

* All employees and contractors of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. with reasonably anticipated occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM) in the performance of their duties, without regard to personal protective equipment
* Job classifications with occupational exposure: Registered Nurse (RN), Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN), Physical Therapist (PT), Occupational Therapist (OT), Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP), Medical Social Worker (MSW), Home Health Aide (HHA), Intake Coordinator (if performing blood glucose or clinical screening)
* All work settings in which clinical procedures involving potential blood/OPIM contact occur: patient residences, community settings, clinical consultation locations

---

## 4. Definitions

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Bloodborne Pathogens | Pathogenic microorganisms present in human blood that can cause disease in humans. The term also applies to any body fluid visibly contaminated with blood; all body fluids involving uncertainty about blood content; semen, vaginal secretions, cerebrospinal fluid, synovial fluid, pleural fluid, peritoneal fluid, pericardial fluid, amniotic fluid; and other OPIM. |
| OPIM | Other Potentially Infectious Materials — includes all body fluids listed in 8 CCR §5193(b)(1)(B) in addition to blood. |
| Occupational Exposure | Reasonably anticipated skin, eye, mucous membrane, or parenteral contact with blood or OPIM that may result from the performance of an employee's duties. |
| Exposure Incident | A specific eye, mouth, other mucous membrane, non-intact skin, or parenteral contact with blood or OPIM that results from the performance of an employee's duties. This is a triggering event for post-exposure evaluation. |
| Universal Precautions | An approach to infection control in which all human blood and certain OPIM are treated as if known to be infectious, regardless of patient diagnosis. (Also referred to as Standard Precautions in contemporary IPC terminology, which is the preferred term.) |
| Engineering Controls | Physical or mechanical measures that isolate or remove the BBP hazard from the workplace, including but not limited to: sharps disposal containers, self-sheathing needles, needleless IV systems, safety-engineered sharps, splash guards. |
| Work Practice Controls | Practices that reduce exposure by altering the manner in which tasks are performed, including no two-hand needle recapping, proper sharps disposal procedures, hand hygiene practices. |
| Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) | Specialized clothing or equipment worn by employees to protect against a hazard. For BBP: gloves, gowns, face shields, masks, eye protection, mouthpieces, resuscitation bags. |
| Sharps Injury Log | The electronic or paper log documenting all sharps injuries per 8 CCR §5193(h)(4), required recording: type and brand of device involved, department/work area, explanation of incident. |
| PLHCP | Physician or Licensed Health Care Professional — the occupational health professional who conducts post-exposure medical evaluation and provides the written opinion. |

---

## 5. Policy Statement

5.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a current, written Bloodborne Pathogen Exposure Control Plan that meets all requirements of 8 CCR §5193 and is accessible to all employees during every work shift.

5.2 The agency shall determine and document which employees have occupational exposure as part of this ECP (see Section 6.1 and Appendix A — BBP Exposure Determination Table).

5.3 The agency shall implement and maintain a schedule of methods to achieve compliance with the BBP standard, applying engineering controls, work practice controls, and PPE in the hierarchy established by 8 CCR §5193(d).

5.4 The agency shall offer the hepatitis B vaccination series at no cost to all employees with occupational exposure, within 10 working days of assignment to a position with occupational exposure, following training, and when the employee is not occupationally contraindicated.

5.5 The agency shall provide post-exposure evaluation and follow-up at no cost to any employee who sustains an exposure incident, within the timeframes specified in Section 6.6.

5.6 The agency shall maintain a sharps injury log (separate from the OSHA 300 Log) that records all sharps injuries in the manner specified in 8 CCR §5193(h)(4), and use the sharps injury log data annually to identify opportunities to implement safer sharps devices.

5.7 The agency shall provide BBP training to all employees with occupational exposure before initial assignment and annually thereafter, meeting the content requirements of 8 CCR §5193(g).

5.8 The agency shall not charge employees for any aspect of the BBP control program: training, PPE, vaccination, post-exposure evaluation, recordkeeping, or this ECP itself.

5.9 Employee BBP exposure medical records shall be maintained confidentially, separate from personnel files, per California CMIA requirements (CO-CA-001) and 8 CCR §5193(h)(1).

5.10 This ECP shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, whenever a task or procedure is modified in a way that affects BBP exposure risk, and whenever safer medical devices become commercially available for tasks performed by agency employees.

---

## 6. Procedures

### 6.1 BBP Exposure Determination

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.1.1 | Director of Nursing / Risk Manager | Complete and maintain the BBP Exposure Determination by job classification (Appendix A), identifying: (a) all job classifications where occupational exposure occurs without regard to protective equipment; (b) all job classifications where occupational exposure occurs in certain tasks only (List 2 — identify specific tasks). | At ECP adoption; review and confirm annually. |
| 6.1.2 | Director of Nursing | For each job classification in List 1 (exposure in all tasks), document the primary exposure pathways (e.g., blood draw, wound care, IV access, suctioning). For List 2, document only the specific tasks creating exposure. Attach as Appendix A. | At adoption; update within 30 days of new service introduction. |
| 6.1.3 | Risk Manager | When a new job task or clinical service is introduced, conduct a supplemental BBP exposure determination for the new activity before any employee performs the task. | Before task introduction. |

### 6.2 Engineering and Work Practice Controls

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.2.1 | Risk Manager / Director of Nursing | Evaluate and implement, to the extent feasible, engineering controls for all sharps procedures performed in patient homes: (a) all IV insertions shall use needleless or safety-engineered IV access systems; (b) all blood draws shall use safety-engineered phlebotomy devices; (c) finger-stick devices shall be self-retracting; (d) all agency-supplied sharps shall be safety-engineered as commercially available. | Prior to ECP effective date; update annually with sharps injury review and device availability. |
| 6.2.2 | Risk Manager | Conduct an annual review of available safety-engineered sharps devices, taking into account: sharps injury log data, frontline employee input, and commercial availability. Document that safer alternatives were considered; if not implemented, document clinical or technical infeasibility. | Annually; documented in annual ECP review. |
| 6.2.3 | All Clinical Staff | Perform all sharps procedures using work practice controls: (a) NEVER recap needles using a two-hand technique; (b) needles may be recapped using a one-hand scoop technique or a mechanical recapping device only when required for safe disposal transport; (c) needles shall never be bent, broken, or removed from disposable syringes by hand; (d) broken glassware shall be handled with mechanical device (forceps, brush), not bare hands; (e) blood or OPIM specimens shall be contained in leak-proof containers. | Every procedure. |
| 6.2.4 | All Clinical Staff | Dispose of all contaminated sharps immediately after use in an agency-supplied, OSHA-compliant sharps disposal container (rigid, puncture-resistant, leak-proof, labeled with the biohazard symbol and the word "BIOHAZARD"). Field staff shall carry a portable sharps container to each visit. | Immediately after each use. |
| 6.2.5 | All Clinical Staff | Wash hands immediately after removing gloves and after any skin contact with blood or OPIM. When handwashing is not immediately available in the field, use ABHR (alcohol-based hand rub) immediately and wash with soap and water as soon as feasible. | After each patient contact involving blood/OPIM. |
| 6.2.6 | All Clinical Staff | Perform mouth-to-mouth resuscitation using a disposable CPR barrier device (pocket mask or face shield) from the agency-issued field supply kit. Never perform unprotected mouth-to-mouth resuscitation. | Whenever CPR is performed. |

### 6.3 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.3.1 | Risk Manager / Agency Supply | Provide all BBP-applicable PPE to employees at no cost: (a) exam gloves (non-latex option available for employees with latex sensitivity); (b) fluid-resistant gowns or aprons for procedures with splash risk; (c) face shields or safety glasses + mask for procedures with OPIM splash/spray risk; (d) surgical masks; (e) CPR barrier devices; (f) portable sharps containers for field use. | PPE available before any employee begins duties with exposure risk; replenished as needed. |
| 6.3.2 | All Clinical Staff | Wear gloves for all anticipated direct contact with blood, OPIM, mucous membranes, non-intact skin, or contaminated surfaces or items. Replace gloves that are torn, punctured, or significantly contaminated. Double-glove when performing procedures with high sharps risk (e.g., complex wound care, IV removal from agitated patient). | Every patient contact involving exposure risk. |
| 6.3.3 | All Clinical Staff | Wear appropriate face and eye protection (face shield or goggles + mask) when performing procedures that create splash or spray of blood or OPIM: suctioning, wound irrigation, IV access in high-pressure lines, bleeding control of arterial sites. | During AGP-type or splash-risk procedures. |
| 6.3.4 | All Clinical Staff | If PPE is penetrated (e.g., glove puncture) or if another mechanism creates potential exposure, report as an Exposure Incident per Section 6.6 immediately. | Immediately. |
| 6.3.5 | Director of Nursing | Evaluate the adequacy of PPE type and availability at least annually by reviewing exposure incident patterns, sharps injury log, and employee feedback. Update the PPE supply protocol accordingly. | Annually. |

### 6.4 Hepatitis B Vaccination Program

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.4.1 | HR / Risk Manager | Offer the HBV vaccine series at no cost to all employees with occupational exposure, as identified in Appendix A. The offer shall be made after BBP training and within 10 working days of initial assignment to an occupationally exposed position. | Within 10 working days of assignment. |
| 6.4.2 | HR | Document the HBV vaccination offer and employee response on the HBV Vaccine Offer/Declination Form (Appendix B). If the employee declines the vaccine, obtain a signed declination statement. Employees who decline may later request vaccination at no cost while still employed in an exposure-risk position. | At time of offer; update if employee later accepts. |
| 6.4.3 | HR | Maintain proof of HBV vaccination series completion (or documented immunity via titer) and signed declination statements in the employee's confidential medical file. | At time of vaccination or declination. |
| 6.4.4 | HR / Risk Manager | After completion of the 3-dose HBV series, offer post-vaccination serology testing (anti-HBs) to verify immune response if employee requests, or in the event of a subsequent occupational HBV exposure (non-immune employees require expedited evaluation). | Per employee request or post-exposure determination. |
| 6.4.5 | HR | Offer HBV booster or revaccination per current CDC guidance when new guidance recommends it, or if a non-immune employee is identified after a prior completed series. | Per CDC/ACIP guidance updates. |

### 6.5 Housekeeping and Decontamination

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.5.1 | Clinical Staff | After any clinical procedure in a patient home involving blood or OPIM: (a) discard all single-use contaminated sharps in the portable sharps container; (b) discard all single-use contaminated PPE in a biohazard waste bag; (c) clean any surface contaminated with blood or OPIM using an appropriate disinfectant (EPA-registered hospital-grade disinfectant active against HIV and HBV) from the agency's approved supply list; (d) seal and return biohazard waste bag from the patient home per agency waste disposal protocol. | After each procedure. |
| 6.5.2 | Risk Manager | Maintain an approved list of EPA-registered disinfectants suitable for blood/OPIM decontamination that field staff are authorized to use. Post the list in the agency office and include in field supply kits. | Maintained continuously; reviewed annually. |
| 6.5.3 | Clinical Staff | Never transport contaminated sharps in soft bags, pockets, or any container not specifically designated as a sharps container. Transport full portable sharps containers sealed per manufacturer instructions to the agency office for proper disposal per agency biomedical waste disposal agreement. | Continuous. |

### 6.6 Exposure Incident Response

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6.6.1 | Exposed Employee | For any exposure incident (needlestick, splash to eye/mucous membrane, broken skin contact with blood/OPIM): (a) immediately wash the affected skin area thoroughly with soap and water; (b) for eye/mucous membrane exposure, flush with clean water for ≥15 minutes; (c) do NOT apply caustic agents, bleach, or anti-infective agents to the wound; (d) report to supervisor and Director of Nursing immediately. | Immediately upon exposure. |
| 6.6.2 | Supervisor / Director of Nursing | Upon receipt of exposure report: (a) confirm initial first aid was performed; (b) contact the agency's designated PLHCP/occupational health provider immediately to arrange same-day post-exposure evaluation; (c) document the exposure circumstances on the BBP Exposure Incident Form (Appendix C). | Within 2 hours of exposure report. |
| 6.6.3 | Risk Manager | Arrange and authorize the employee's post-exposure evaluation at no cost. The evaluation must include: (a) documentation of the route and circumstances of exposure; (b) identification of the source patient, if possible, with source patient testing (with consent per California law — CMIA requirements apply); (c) HIV baseline testing of exposed employee; (d) HBV and HCV baseline testing; (e) assessment for HIV PEP if indicated (must commence within 72 hours); (f) PLHCP written opinion within 15 days of evaluation. | Same-day evaluation arranged by supervisor. PEP assessment within 2–4 hours if HIV source risk. |
| 6.6.4 | Risk Manager | If the source patient is known or suspected to have HIV: ensure the employee is informed of the availability of HIV PEP and that PEP must begin within 72 hours for maximum effectiveness. Ensure the occupational health provider assesses PEP eligibility. | Within 2 hours of determining source HIV status. |
| 6.6.5 | Risk Manager | Receive the PLHCP written opinion within 15 business days of the evaluation and provide a copy to the employee. The opinion shall state only: (a) whether HBV vaccine is indicated and was provided; (b) that the employee was informed of results and any necessary follow-up. The written opinion shall NOT include the employee's diagnosis, specific HIV/HBV/HCV test results, or other medical information. | Within 15 days of evaluation; provide copy to employee. |
| 6.6.6 | Risk Manager | Document the exposure incident in the Sharps Injury Log (Appendix D) if it involved a sharp device, per 8 CCR §5193(h)(4). Record: type and brand of device, department/work area (patient home visit), and explanation of incident. Log shall be de-identified before any aggregate review by personnel other than the Responsible Person. | Within 7 days of incident. |
| 6.6.7 | Risk Manager | Record any work-related BBP illness on the OSHA 300 Log per RM-OS-001. Report to Cal/OSHA immediately if the exposure results in hospitalization or death. | Per RM-OS-001 recordkeeping requirements. |
| 6.6.8 | Risk Manager / Director of Nursing | Conduct a post-exposure Root Cause Analysis per QA-AE-002 to determine contributing factors, including whether engineering controls were in place and used, whether PPE was available and used, and whether a safer device could have prevented the exposure. Update ECP and device selection within 30 days of RCA completion. | RCA within 14 days; ECP update within 30 days. |

### 6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

| Condition | Escalation Path | Corrective Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Employee refuses HBV vaccine and will not sign declination | HR Director and Risk Manager notified. | Employee may continue occupational exposure duties but risk is documented. HR documents employee's refusal of agency's safety program offering. | Within 5 business days. |
| Source patient for exposure incident refuses blood test | PLHCP and Risk Manager assess baseline exposure risk from alternative information. | Post-exposure management proceeds based on clinical risk assessment per current CDC/OSHA guidance. | Within 24 hours of refusal. |
| HIV PEP supply unavailable through standard provider | Risk Manager escalates to Administrator, contacts alternative occupational health or emergency department. | Ensure employee reaches PEP-capable provider within 72-hour window regardless of standard provider availability. | Within 2 hours of supply/access issue identification. |
| Annual ECP review identifies safer sharps device commercially available | Risk Manager documents the device, evaluates feasibility. | If feasible, transition to safer device within 90 days. If not feasible, document clinical rationale in writing. | 90 days for implementation; immediate documentation of decision. |

## 8. Compliance & Audit Considerations

### 8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

| Compliance Indicator | Measurement Method | Acceptable Standard |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Written BBP ECP exists, current, and accessible | Annual review against 8 CCR §5193 checklist | All required elements present; reviewed within 12 months |
| BBP Exposure Determination current | Review of Appendix A | All job classifications assessed; reviewed annually |
| HBV vaccine offered within 10 working days of assignment | HR file audit — verify offer date vs. assignment date | 100% within 10 working days |
| Declination statements on file for employees who declined HBV vaccine | HR medical file audit | 100% of declined employees have signed declination form |
| All exposure incidents have PLHCP written opinion within 15 days | Review of Appendix C files | 100% within 15 days |
| Sharps injury log maintained | Review of Appendix D log | All sharps injuries documented; log reviewed annually for device review |
| BBP training completed annually | Training completion rate | 100% within calendar year |
| BBP medical records in confidential medical file (not personnel file) | HR file audit | 100% separate and access-controlled |

### 8.2 What Surveyors and Auditors Will Look For

Cal/OSHA compliance officers will specifically verify:

1. The written BBP ECP is available at the workplace. The ECP must be accessible to employees throughout each work shift.
2. The Exposure Determination identifies specific job classifications and tasks with occupational exposure without regard to PPE.
3. Engineering controls are being used and the annual review of safer needle devices is documented with employee input.
4. The HBV vaccination program is being offered within 10 working days, and declination forms are on file.
5. Post-exposure evaluation and follow-up procedures were followed for any documented incidents, and PLHCP written opinions are on file.
6. The Sharps Injury Log is maintained separately from the OSHA 300 Log, and the log has been reviewed annually for safer device opportunities.
7. BBP medical records are in a separate confidential medical file, not the general personnel file.

CMS surveys may cross-check against CL-SD-016 (IPC) and HR-WM-003 (immunizations) for cross-compliance evidence.

### 8.3 Common Failure Points

| Failure Point | Risk | Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| No annual safer sharps device review with employee input | Cal/OSHA §5193(d)(2)(B) requires annual review with frontline input | Annual device review meeting with clinical staff documented; findings in ECP file |
| HBV vaccine not offered within 10 working days | Cal/OSHA citation | HR onboarding checklist includes HBV offer as Day 1–10 action item |
| Exposure incident response not initiated same-day | Loss of PEP window (72 hours for HIV) | 24/7 supervisor reporting protocol; occupational health provider on retainer for after-hours exposure evaluation |
| BBP records filed in personnel file | CMIA violation; Cal/OSHA violation | Separate medical file per CO-CA-001; HR-WM-007 training reinforces separation |
| No sharps injury log since "no injuries occurred" | Cal/OSHA citation — log must be maintained to record any incidents | Log maintained with zero entries when applicable; available for inspection |
